memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Appoint three men from each tribe. I will send them out to make a survey of the land and to write a description of it, according to the inheritance of each. Then they will return to me. You are to divide the land into seven parts. Judah is to remain in its territory on the south and the tribes of Joseph in their territory on the north" - Josh 18:4-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joshua does not simply tell the tribes to rush out blindly. He gives them a plan: appoint men, survey the land, write a careful description, then divide it fairly. Faith and wisdom work together here. Taking possession of God's promise involved thoughtful preparation, not reckless haste. They were to look, measure, record, and then act.

There is a healthy balance in this. Sometimes we imagine that trusting God means acting without any planning, as though preparation shows a lack of faith. But Joshua models something different: trust in God expressed through careful, wise action. The men were sent to survey precisely because the tribes were meant to take the land — the planning served the faith, it did not replace it.

This is a helpful pattern for our own walk with God. Stepping into what He has given often involves prayerful thought, honest assessment, and practical preparation. We survey the ground, count the cost, and make our plans — all while trusting God for the outcome. Wisdom and faith are not enemies; they are partners. The God who calls us forward also gives us minds to plan and prepare. We commit our ways to Him and He directs our steps, working through both our trust and our thoughtful effort (Prov 16:3, 9).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you tend to act rashly, or to over-plan and never step out?
- How can faith and careful preparation work together in your decisions?
- What "survey" might God be asking you to do before stepping forward?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to hold faith and wisdom together — trusting You fully while planning and preparing thoughtfully. Direct my steps as I commit my ways to You. Amen.
